title: Beyond Semantic Similarity: A Component-Wise Evaluation Framework for Medical Question Answering Systems with Health Equity Implications

bias_targets.methodology: Comparing model performance on medical question answering (using the multi-component VB-Score framework) across different public health topics, specifically contrasting performance on infectious diseases versus chronic conditions.

Evaluating the downstream equity impact of condition-based performance disparities on elderly populations (65+), demonstrating that age groups with a higher prevalence of chronic diseases receive systematically lower-quality AI-generated health information.

Linking algorithmic underperformance on chronic disease topics to racial and ethnic minority populations (e.g., African American and Hispanic communities) to demonstrate an indirect form of bias driven by historical patterns of chronic disease burden.

Mapping the condition-based AI performance gaps to low-income communities, showing how poorer factual consistency and entity recognition for chronic diseases disproportionately impact economically vulnerable populations.
